title: Go SDK: handle connection races and cancel-safety for streaming API
creator: Aisha Rao
description:
Goal: make the Go SDK's streaming client resilient to race conditions between network disconnects and user-initiated cancellation/timeouts, and provide clear ergonomics/examples for customers.

Background: we've seen a few customer-reported flakes where long-running streams leak goroutines or hang when a caller cancels a context concurrently with a server-side close or network interruption. Current implementation tends to race between Read/Write loops, context cancel handlers, and transport-level Close, resulting in: leaked goroutines in the client's read loop, opaque errors returned to callers, and unclear patterns for users about when to cancel vs. set request deadlines.

This ticket implements a robust pattern that: 1) ensures a single point of stream shutdown (closeOnce), 2) coordinates cancellation with transport Close to avoid double-closing or canceled-while-reading races, 3) surfaces deterministic error values (ErrStreamCanceled, ErrStreamClosed, ErrTransportFailed) for callers, and 4) documents recommended usage patterns and examples (graceful cancel, aggressive timeout, resume semantics).

Non-goals: changing server-side protocol semantics, adding end-to-end resumable sessions in this ticket (follow-up), or reworking higher-level public APIs beyond backward-compatible helpers and examples.
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests that simulate cancellation racing with packet loss and ensure no goroutine leaks
Integration test against flaky proxy (tcpkill-style) validates deterministic error surface for canceled vs transport failures
SDK examples doc updated with three patterns: (1) graceful cancel after receiving N tokens, (2) context-with-deadline for short timeouts, (3) explicit CloseAfter with drain/timeout
No increase in CI flakiness for streaming test matrix after landing (monitor for 48h)
work_items: Spike: reproduce leak with test harness using net.Pipe + goroutine watchdog (done)
Refactor: introduce stream.shutdown channel and sync.Once close path (in PR)
Add: canonical error types and exported helper functions (in PR)
Docs: add examples in SDK README and examples/streaming/cancelation.go (draft)
Tests: flaky-proxy integration job + unit tests for race windows (in progress)
updates: 2026-03-10 - Aisha Rao: Created ticket after customer P1 report (support-2984). Initial spike completed: reproduced leak locally using a simulated mid-stream EOF while context was canceled. Repro details uploaded to Drive: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1a2b3c-spike-stream-race

2026-03-11 - Liam Carter: Implemented close coordination using a shutdown channel and sync.Once; added exported ErrStreamCanceled/ErrStreamClosed constants. Opened PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/pull/4391

2026-03-11 - Design review by Priya Kulkarni: Confirmed public ergonomics — keep existing Stream.Read API but add helper Stream.CloseWithDrain(ctx, timeout) and example code. Asked to add clear docs about when to use context cancellation vs CloseWithDrain.

2026-03-12 - QA (Diego Morales): Added integration harness to simulate TCP reset mid-read. Found case where cancellation after transport Close produced wrapped net.OpError; added mapping to ErrTransportFailed. Added test cases to PR. Running full CI.
2026-03-12 - Liam Carter: Addressed PR feedback: removed reliance on runtime.SetFinalizer, added explicit goroutine tracking in tests, documented expected error return semantics in README.
Next: Monitor CI and rollout as minor SDK patch (0.8.3) after merge. Follow-up ticket to add resumable streams and server-side session tokens.
testing_plan: Unit: deterministic goroutine watchdog that fails test if goroutines leak after context cancel; simulate transport closure and ensure stream shutdown path runs. Integration: flaky-proxy job that resets TCP connection at random offsets during stream to validate error mapping. E2E: small app that uses Stream.CloseWithDrain(ctx, 200ms) under load and compares behavior to context-with-deadline pattern. Add CI job that runs these tests under race detector.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: behavioral change in error values may break existing callers that introspect error strings. Mitigation: keep legacy error text for a deprecation window and publish migration note in CHANGELOG. Risk: subtle deadlocks if CloseWithDrain is misused; mitigation: defensive timeouts and clear docs + runtime checks.
